name: Jane Austen
biography: English novelist known for her social commentary in novels including Pride and Prejudice.

name: Mary Shelley
biography: English novelist who wrote the Gothic novel Frankenstein.

name: H. G. Wells
biography: English writer. Prolific in many genres, he wrote dozens of novels, short stories, and works of social commentary.

name: Arthur Conan Doyle
biography: British writer and physician, most noted for creating the fictional detective Sherlock Holmes.

name: Bram Stoker
biography: Irish author, best known today for his 1897 Gothic horror novel Dracula.

name: Oscar Wilde
biography: Irish poet and playwright. After writing in different forms throughout the 1880s, he became one of London's most popular playwrights in the early 1890s.

name: L. Frank Baum
biography: American author chiefly known for his children's books, particularly The Wonderful Wizard of Oz.

name: Mark Twain
biography: American writer, humorist, entrepreneur, publisher, and lecturer.

name: Charles Dickens
biography: English writer and social critic. He created some of the world's best-known fictional characters.

name: Frances Hodgson Burnett
biography: British-American novelist and playwright. She is best known for the three children's novels Little Lord Fauntleroy, A Little Princess, and The Secret Garden.

name: Louisa May Alcott
biography: American novelist and poet best known as the author of the novel Little Women.

name: Alexandre Dumas
biography: French writer. His works have been translated into many languages, and he is one of the most widely read French authors.

name: Robert Louis Stevenson
biography: Scottish novelist and travel writer, most noted for Treasure Island, Kidnapped, and Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.

name: Charlotte Brontë
biography: English novelist and poet, the eldest of the three Brontë sisters who survived into adulthood and whose novels became classics of English literature.

name: Herman Melville
biography: American novelist, short story writer, and poet of the American Renaissance period.
